land.text: Kabul and its surroundings within about 160 km, with Ghazni, the Sadozai rump that the Barakzai took in March 1823

predecessors.note: The Emirate page's infobox also lists the Herat State, the Principality of Kandahar, the Maimana Khanate, the Kunduz Khanate and the Mirdom of Badakhshan as predecessors; they were absorbed later (Kandahar 1855, Herat 1863, the north 1849-1859 by the page set's silence) and are in the ledger, not at the birth.

land.text: the Emirate's whole territory: 'Amanullah reformed the country as the Kingdom of Afghanistan in 1926' (infobox 'Transformed into a kingdom: 9 June 1926')

successors.note: Cliopatria starts the Kingdom of Afghanistan in 1926.

capitals.name: Ghazni (de facto)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ghazni (de facto, 1879-1880)', while the British held Kabul (Roberts occupied it in October 1879).

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: Back at Kabul with Abdur Rahman (Amir from 11 August 1880).

rulers.name: Habibullah Khan
rulers.note: The rulers table gives 1823-1823, the infobox 1823-1824; overthrown by his uncle Yar Mohammad Khan.

rulers.name: Dost Mohammad Khan
rulers.note: First reign, 6 May 1834 to 2 August 1839; 'Sardar of Kabul' from 1826 and Emir of Kabul by 1834 (his own page also says 1825).

rulers.name: Dost Mohammad Khan
rulers.note: Restored April 1843; 'Emir of Afghanistan' from 30 November 1855 to his death at Herat on 9 June 1863. Shuja Shah ruled at Kabul under the British from August 1839 to April 1842 (durrani-dynasty).

rulers.name: Sher Ali Khan
rulers.note: 9 June 1863 to 10 May 1866; second reign 8 September 1868 to 21 February 1879.

rulers.name: Mohammad Yaqub Khan
rulers.note: 21 February to 19 October 1879; he signed the Treaty of Gandamak.

rulers.name: Nasrullah Khan
rulers.note: The page lists him to 28 February 1919 with a start date (19 October 1879) that conflicts with the rest of the table; reign taken as the days after Habibullah's death.

rulers.name: Amanullah Khan
rulers.note: Took power in 1919 per the text (the table's start date conflicts); king from 9 June 1926.

region.text: Kabul and Ghazni, the Principality of Kabul

ledger.note: 1823: the Barakzai take Kabul. 'Established: 1823' (infobox, 'Predecessor: Durrani Empire'); 'Kabul fell in March 1823, and the Barakzai dynasty superseded the Durranis' (Durrani Empire page). The page gives the year; the land is the Durrani page's 'Kabul and its surroundings within about 160 km' with Ghazni.

region.text: the Peshawar valley and the Khyber approach

ledger.note: 1834: Peshawar. While Dost Mohammad 'marched on Kandahar, Ranjit Singh seized the opportunity to annex Peshawar'; the Sikh Empire page says Peshawar was 'formally annexed in 1834'. The Khyber standoff followed (1834-35).
1834: the Principality of Kabul becomes an emirate. Status 'Principality (1823-1834); Emirate (1834-1926)'; Dost Mohammad's first reign as Emir of Kabul begins 6 May 1834 (infobox of his page).

30 April 1837: Jamrud. Akbar Khan was sent 'to defeat the Sikhs at the Battle of Jamrud in 1837'; 'the final battle was fought on 30 April 1837', the last Afghan-Sikh confrontation on the Sikh western boundary (Sikh Empire page). Peshawar stays Sikh.

region.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan)

ledger.note: August 1839: Dost Mohammad is deposed. 'The British marched to Kabul with no resistance from Dost Mohammad's troops'; 'in August 1839, after thirty years, Shuja was again enthroned in Kabul' (his reign ends 2 August 1839, infobox). The British took Kandahar on 25 April and Ghazni on 23 July 1839.

region.text: Kabul and its surroundings as before 1839

ledger.note: April 1843: Dost Mohammad returns. 'Restoration, April 1843' (infobox); 'Emir of Kabul (2nd reign): April 1843' (Dost page, which has him exiled to Mussoorie in November 1840). Shuja was murdered in April 1842, Fateh Jang left with the British in October 1842 and Shahpur's reign 'ended with the return of Dost Mohammad Khan from exile' (First Anglo-Afghan War page).

region.text: Tashqurghan (Khulm) and the Uzbek begs south of the Amu Darya

ledger.note: 1850: Tashqurghan (Khulm). 'In 1850 Ghulam Haidar Khan conquered Tashqurghan'; Mohammad Akram Khan had been sent 'to invade Balkh in the Spring of 1849'. The page does not say Balkh itself was taken; the Emirate page lists the Kunduz Khanate, Maimana Khanate and Mirdom of Badakhshan as predecessors without dates. The Bukhara page says the Chahar Wilayat 'nominally accepted Bukharan suzerainty' in the first half of the century.

30 November 1855: Dost Mohammad becomes 'Emir of Afghanistan' after Kandahar (infobox 'Emir of Afghanistan: 30 November 1855 - 9 June 1863'); the Emirate page names the state 'Emirate of Kabul (until 1855)'.

region.text: the Principality of Kandahar with the Western Frontier (Garmsir, Zamindawar, Deh Rawood, Uruzgan)

ledger.note: November 1855: Kandahar. 'In November 1855, he conquered Kandahar.' The Principality of Kandahar page puts the conquest in 'September 1856' after Kohan Dil Khan's death; the two pages disagree and the Cliopatria 1856 shape does not settle it.

27 May 1863: Herat. 'On May 27 Dost Mohammad made a final assault on Herat' after a ten-month siege; the city 'was conquered by the Emirate of Afghanistan, ending the Principality of Herat'. He died there on 9 June 1863; the civil war between his sons followed (Emirate page: 'unification and civil war, 9 June 1863').

region.text: Kabul, Kandahar and the Khyber approach

ledger.note: 21 November 1878: the Second Anglo-Afghan War. 'The first campaign began in November 1878'; infobox '21 November 1878 - 27 April 1881'. The British took the Khyber, Kurram and Kandahar fronts and occupied Kabul in October 1879.
1879: the capital moves de facto to Ghazni ('Ghazni (de facto, 1879-1880)') while the British hold Kabul after Cavagnari's murder on 3 September 1879 and Roberts's occupation in October.

region.text: the districts of Quetta, Pishin, Sibi, Harnai and Thal Chotiali, and the Khyber and Michni passes (Cliopatria drops 79 Pakistan-side cells in 1880)

ledger.note: 26 May 1879: Treaty of Gandamak. Yaqub Khan 'gave up control of Afghan foreign affairs to Britain'; 'Districts of Quetta, Pishin, Sibi, Harnai & Thal Chotiali ceded to British India' (infobox) and 'control was extended to the Khyber and Michni passes'. The Emirate page gives 24 May in its infobox and 26 May in the text.
1880: the court is back at Kabul with Abdur Rahman, 'officially recognized as Amir' on 22 July 1880 and Emir from 11 August 1880.

region.text: Kabul, Kandahar and the Khyber approach

ledger.note: April 1881: the British leave. Infobox end '27 April 1881' (the text says March 1881); 'in 1881, the British troops also handed over Kandahar to the new Amir' (Abdur Rahman page).

region.text: the Panjdeh oasis on the Murghab and the Zulfikar pass

ledger.note: 30 March 1885: Panjdeh. 'Russians attacked the Afghans and defeated them, putting them to flight' (the battle of Kushka); the Afghan Boundary Commission, which ran 1884-1888, 'started at Zulfikar on 10 November' and 'reached the Murghab by Christmas'.

1885: Panjdeh is lost. 'Russia cedes Zu'l Faqar but retains Panjdeh' (infobox); 'by 10 September, it was roughly agreed that Russia would keep Panjdeh'. Cliopatria's shape already ends on the modern northern border, so it does not show the loss.

region.text: the Panjdeh oasis and the Zulfikar pass

ledger.note: 22 July 1887: 'the final protocol was signed on 22 July 1887' fixing the northern frontier west of the Oxus.

region.text: Asmar in the Kunar valley and the Chitral frontier lands (the cells Cliopatria adds in 1895)

ledger.note: 12 November 1893: the Durand Line. The Agreement 'granted Nuristan (then known as Kafiristan) and parts of Chitral to Afghanistan' and 'Asmar in Kunar Valley as far as Chanak was ceded to Afghanistan', 'giving up claims to Waziristan and Chageh'; it 'created Wakhan Corridor as buffer'. Demarcation ran 1894-96.

region.text: Nasrat, Bashgal and the other areas ceded at Nashagam

ledger.note: 1895: Nashagam. 'Nasrat and Bashgal, along with other areas, were ceded to Afghanistan' (Durand Line page); the Domandi-Chaman section was signed by 26 February 1895.
1896: Kafiristan. 'In 1895-1896, Abdur Rahman directed the invasion of Kafiristan and the conversion of its indigenous peoples to Islam'; the region was renamed Nuristan.
9 June 1926: the Emirate becomes a kingdom. 'Amanullah reformed the country as the Kingdom of Afghanistan in 1926' (infobox 'Transformed into a kingdom: 9 June 1926').

correction.text: Kabul within about 160 km and Ghazni

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Emirate in 1828 but the page has 'Established: 1823', with the principality of Kabul under Habibullah and Yar Mohammad Khan (1823-26) and Dost Mohammad holding Ghazni ('Dost received Ghazni, and in 1826 he added Kabul'). Cliopatria's 1822 and 1825 Durrani shapes for these years are outlines of modern Afghanistan plus Peshawar and Gilgit; the Durrani page puts the Sadozai at 'little more than Kabul and its surroundings within about 160 km'. The Peshawar valley went to the Sikhs as a tributary on 14 March 1823.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan)

keyframe_review.note: 0.88 M km2 (Cliopatria) is the outline of modern Afghanistan plus Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit and 17% of Indian Kashmir. The Emirate page gives no area for a check. The Dost Mohammad page has the Barakzai at Kabul and Ghazni only: 'in 1826 he added Kabul', the Peshawar valley lost 'in March 1823' at Nowshera, Kandahar a separate principality from August 1818 under the Dil brothers and Herat a separate principality from 1793 to 1863 (Herat page). Kafiristan (Nuristan) was invaded only in 1895-96. The north (Balkh, Kunduz, Faryab, Badakhshan) is left in as unverified: page budget; the page lists the Maimana Khanate, the Kunduz Khanate and the Mirdom of Badakhshan as separate states and Dost sent Akram Khan against Balkh only in spring 1849.

keyframe_review.note: 0.82 M km2. Dost Mohammad took the title in May 1834 (infobox 6 May 1834); while he marched on Kandahar 'Ranjit Singh seized the opportunity to annex Peshawar' (formally annexed in 1834, Sikh Empire page). Cliopatria drops its Kashmir slice in 1834, which was never Afghan after 1819. Same corrections as 1828.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan)

keyframe_review.note: 0.79 M km2: Cliopatria's eastern frontier is pulled back (110 cells of Pakistani border land west of the Indus, centred at 70E 30N) in 1836, the year before 'the final battle ... on 30 April 1837' at Jamrud against the Sikhs. Same corrections as 1828.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan); the same land as Cliopatria's 1846 Emirate shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Emirate shape for 1840-1845 (it gives the Durrani Dynasty row 1840-1845, i.e. Shuja's British-backed restoration, which ended in 1842). Dost Mohammad was released and returned: 'restoration, April 1843' (infobox), 'Emir of Kabul (2nd reign): April 1843'. The Principality of Kandahar was 're-established following the deposition of Durranis and British soldiers from Kandahar' under Kohan Dil Khan. Shape = the 1846 shape with the corrections.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan)

keyframe_review.note: 0.67 M km2 from 1846: Cliopatria's shape is now exactly modern Afghanistan (99% of the country). The Emirate page has no area. Until November 1855 Kandahar was Kohan Dil Khan's principality ('conquered ... in November 1855', Dost page; 'September 1856', Principality of Kandahar page) and until 27 May 1863 Herat a separate state; Kafiristan only fell in 1895-96. Same corrections as 1828.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan and without the independent principalities of Kandahar (with Helmand and Uruzgan) and Herat and without Kafiristan (Nuristan)

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as 1846 (665,776 km2). Balkh: 'Mohammad Akram Khan invaded Balkh in the Spring of 1849' and 'in 1850 Ghulam Haidar Khan conquered Tashqurghan' (Dost page); the outcome at Balkh is not stated, and Cliopatria already holds the north from 1828. Kandahar joins in November 1855 (ledger). Same corrections as 1828.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan, without Herat and without Kafiristan; Kandahar included (conquered November 1855)

keyframe_review.note: 0.64 M km2: Cliopatria removes 57% of Herat province for 1856 only, the Persian occupation ('On October 25, 1856, Herat fell to the Iranian forces'), as if Herat were Emirate land. It was the Principality of Herat's, not the Emirate's, until 27 May 1863. Kandahar is included here from November 1855 (Dost page; the Kandahar page says September 1856).

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape cut to modern Afghanistan, without Herat (until 27 May 1863) and without Kafiristan

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1846 (665,776 km2). Persian forces left Herat in September 1857 but it stayed a separate principality until Dost Mohammad's assault of 27 May 1863; the corrected shape is the state in 1857-1862, and the ledger adds Herat in 1863. The Anglo-Persian war ended with a Treaty of Paris that 'forbade Iran to interfere in the affairs of Herat'.

Same extent (665,849 km2). The Emirate page has no area. Kafiristan (Nuristan) was invaded in 1895-96 and is taken out until then; the frontier lands on the Pakistan side (about 5% of Peshawar) are the Emirate's until Gandamak (26 May 1879).

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Kafiristan (Nuristan), which Abdur Rahman invaded in 1895-96

keyframe_review.note: 0.644 M km2: the shape drops 79 cells on the Pakistan side (Khyber, Kurram and the passes) at 1880, matching Gandamak (26 May 1879): 'control was extended to the Khyber and Michni passes' and, per the infobox, 'Districts of Quetta, Pishin, Sibi, Harnai & Thal Chotiali ceded to British India'. Panjdeh was lost to Russia in 1885; the Cliopatria shape already ends on the modern northern border. Kafiristan taken out until 1896.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Kafiristan (Nuristan), which enters in 1896

keyframe_review.note: 0.644 M km2: a few cells appear on the Kunar side (Asmar, Bashgal) in 1895, matching the Durand Line: 'Asmar in Kunar Valley as far as Chanak was ceded to Afghanistan' (Agreement of 12 November 1893) and at Nashagam in 1895 'Nasrat and Bashgal ... were ceded to Afghanistan'. Nuristan joins in 1896 (ledger). The Pamir and Wakhan frontier of 1895 is not on the opened pages.

0.644 M km2, unchanged: the final frontier of the emirate. 'De jure British protected state (1879-1919)': Habibullah II ruled to 20 February 1919 and the Anglo-Afghan Treaty of 8 August 1919 gave 'full autonomy'; no land changed hands.
0.644 M km2, unchanged after the 1919 treaty and the November 1921 treaty that finalised the Rawalpindi arrangements and demarcated the Khyber section (Durand Line page).
0.644 M km2, unchanged to the end; the Emirate became the Kingdom of Afghanistan on 9 June 1926.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1925 shape, unchanged, for 1926 until 9 June

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Emirate lasts until 9 June 1926 ('Transformed into a kingdom: 9 June 1926') but Cliopatria's last Emirate shape is 1925; its Kingdom of Afghanistan row begins in 1926. The shape is Cliopatria's 1925 shape unchanged.

wars.name: Sikh-Afghan clashes over Peshawar
wars.outcome: Sikh victory: Peshawar was 'formally annexed in 1834'; the last battle, at Jamrud on 30 April 1837, did not retake it.
wars.note: Dost Mohammad's page: 'Standoff at the Khyber Pass (1834-1835)'.

wars.name: First Anglo-Afghan War

zones.text: Kandahar, Ghazni and Kabul, held by the British 1839-1842

wars.outcome: Barakzai victory (infobox): the British put Shuja on the throne in August 1839, were driven out after the uprising of 2 November 1841 and the retreat of January 1842, and left in October 1842; Dost Mohammad returned in April 1843.
wars.note: Simla Declaration 1 October 1838; Dost Mohammad exiled to India in November 1840.

wars.name: Dost Mohammad's wars of unification
wars.outcome: Balkh invaded in 1849, Tashqurghan taken in 1850, Kandahar conquered in November 1855 and Herat on 27 May 1863; 'he had reunited the principalities of Kandahar and Herat with Kabul'.

wars.name: Anglo-Persian War (1856-1857)
wars.outcome: Persia took Herat on 25 October 1856; after the Treaty of Paris the Iranian forces evacuated in September 1857 and Herat stayed a separate principality. Dost Mohammad 'declared war on Persia in conjunction with the British' in 1857.

wars.name: Afghan civil war of the sons of Dost Mohammad
wars.outcome: Sher Ali (1863-66), Afzal (1866-67), Azam (1867-68) and Sher Ali again from 8 September 1868; the page gives the rulers' dates, not the fronts.
wars.note: Territorial effects not on the opened pages; no events recorded.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Afghan War

zones.text: Kabul, Kandahar and the Khyber approach

wars.outcome: British military victory: Gandamak (26 May 1879) ceded Quetta, Pishin, Sibi, Harnai and Thal Chotiali and gave Britain control of Afghan foreign affairs; the British left in March-April 1881 and Abdur Rahman was recognised on 22 July 1880.

wars.name: Panjdeh incident
wars.outcome: Russia attacked on 30 March 1885 and kept Panjdeh, ceding Zulfikar; the final protocol was signed on 22 July 1887.

wars.name: Hazara revolt against Abdur Rahman
wars.outcome: The page says only 'In the early 1890s Hazaras revolted against Abdur Rahman'; no territorial change is dated.
wars.note: Years are the page's 'early 1890s'; no event recorded.

wars.name: Conquest of Kafiristan
wars.outcome: Abdur Rahman invaded Kafiristan in 1895-96 and converted its peoples to Islam; the Durand Line agreement had already assigned it to Afghanistan.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Afghan War
wars.outcome: Amanullah signed the Anglo-Afghan Treaty of 8 August 1919 and gained 'full autonomy' (end of the British protected-state status); Afghanistan accepted the Durand Line in the treaty.
wars.note: The war itself is not described on the pages opened; no territorial change.

certainty.note: The Sikh frontier at Peshawar and the Khyber, the independent principalities of Kandahar (to 1855) and Herat (to 1863), and the northern begs are approximate.

Sharp from the Durand Line Agreement of 12 November 1893 (demarcated 1894-96, Quetta-Chaman by 1895), the Russian frontier fixed by the protocol of 22 July 1887, and the 1919/1921 treaties; parts of the Durand Line (Bajaur, Mohmand) were never demarcated.

notes: Cliopatria's Emirate of Afghanistan row (1828..1925) is modern Afghanistan from 1846 and a larger Afghanistan-plus-Peshawar-and-Gilgit outline in 1828-1845; the Wikipedia page dates the Emirate from 1823 to the kingdom on 9 June 1926. Corrections made from the pages: Kandahar (Principality of Kandahar, August 1818 to 1855/56), Herat (Principality of Herat, 1793 to 27 May 1863) and Kafiristan (to 1895-96) removed from the early shapes; the Persian dip in the 1856 shape is a Herat artefact; the Peshawar valley, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit are out of every shape before 1879. Not settled within the page budget: the absorption of the north (Balkh, Aqcha, Kunduz, Faryab/Maimana, Badakhshan) between 1849 and the 1880s, which the page set dates only for Tashqurghan 1850; Hazarajat (early 1890s revolt only); the Pamir and Wakhan frontier of 1895; the Dokalim seizure of 1912; Sistan. Those parts of the north are left inside the 1828-1855 shapes as unverified. Page conflicts: Kabul taken by Dost Mohammad in 1826 (his page) against Yar Mohammad Khan ruling 1823-1826 (Emirate rulers table); Kandahar conquered November 1855 (Dost Mohammad page) against September 1856 (Principality of Kandahar page); Gandamak signed 24 May (Emirate infobox) or 26 May 1879 (text and Second Anglo-Afghan War page); the Emirate page's infobox has no area, so no area check was possible. The British protected-state relation (the Emirate page: 'De jure British protected state (1879-1919)') and the British occupation of 1839-42 and 1878-81 belong in the british-raj and british-empire ledgers as vassal and occupation events; this dossier records them only as contest events. Counterparts needing dossiers: principality-of-kandahar (1818-1855/6), principality-of-herat (1793-1863), maimana-khanate, khanate-of-kunduz and mirdom-of-badakhshan (Cliopatria lacks all five). Page budget: 9 pages were opened for this state (Emirate of Afghanistan, Dost Mohammad, First and Second Anglo-Afghan Wars, Abdur Rahman, Durand Line, Panjdeh, Principality of Kandahar, Principality of Herat); the Sikh Empire, Nowshera, Durrani Empire and Emirate of Bukhara pages were opened for neighbouring dossiers and are reused. The Third Anglo-Afghan War page was not opened (budget). Gazetteer: 'Hilmand', 'Hirat', 'Nuristan', 'Samangan', 'Ghazni', 'Quetta' used as found; Panjdeh has no place name and is a 60 km radius around 62.3E 35.7N; Asmar, Bashgal, Wakhan, Hazarajat, Kurram, Pishin and Chitral are not in the gazetteer.
